# Pyreon

> Signal-based UI framework for TypeScript: fine-grained reactivity, standard JSX, SPA, SSR, SSG, ISR and islands on the web, and one source compiled to SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose. Every package is published under `@pyreon/*`.

This file is an index in the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org/) format: each package links to its generated API reference, and [llms-full.txt](https://pyreon.dev/llms-full.txt) holds the complete reference inline (code examples, the full list of common mistakes, every package API). The [@pyreon/mcp](https://pyreon.dev/docs/mcp) server answers the same questions live inside an editor.

The rules that trip up newcomers most often:

- Signals are functions: `count()` reads, `count.set(v)` and `count.update(fn)` write. Calling `count(5)` does NOT write, and there is no `.value`.
- Components run once. Reactivity lives in JSX expressions, `effect()` and `computed()`, so an early `if (cond()) return …` in a component body is static; use `<Show when={() => cond()}>` instead.
- Destructuring props (`const { x } = props`) or a context value captures it once. Read `props.x`, or use `splitProps` / `mergeProps`.
- Lists: `<For each={items()} by={(item) => item.id}>`; the key prop is `by`, not `key`. Attributes are `class` and `for`, not `className` / `htmlFor`; use `onInput` for per-keystroke updates.
- Never nest `effect()` calls; derive values with `computed()`. `.peek()` inside an effect or computed reads without tracking.
- Wrap the app in `<PyreonUI theme={theme} mode="system">` from `@pyreon/ui-core`; it is the only provider the UI system needs.
- Dev-only warnings in library code use the bare `process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'` gate, which every modern bundler replaces and tree-shakes.

- [Recipes](https://pyreon.dev/docs/recipes): Copy-paste solutions to common tasks.

- [MCP server](https://pyreon.dev/docs/mcp): Live API lookup, validation, migration and diagnostics for AI coding assistants (`bunx @pyreon/mcp`).

## Core framework

- [@pyreon/reactivity](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/reactivity): Fine-grained reactivity: signal, computed, linked, effect, batch, onCleanup, createStore, watch, createResource, untrack. Pyreon signals are NOT `.value` getters (Vue ref) or `[state, setState]` tuples (React useState). The signal IS the function: `count()` reads, `count.set(v)` writes, `count.update(fn)` derives. This is the #1 confusion for developers coming from other frameworks.
- [@pyreon/core](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/core): VNode, h(), Fragment, lifecycle, context, JSX runtime, Suspense, ErrorBoundary, lazy(), Dynamic, cx(), splitProps, mergeProps, createUniqueId. Pyreon components are plain functions that execute a single time. Reactivity comes from reading signals inside reactive scopes (JSX expression thunks, `effect()`, `computed()`), not from re-running the component function. `if (!cond()) return null` at the top level runs once and is static — use `return (() => { if (!cond()) return null; return <div /> })` for reactive conditional rendering.
- [@pyreon/compiler](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/compiler): JSX reactive transform (Rust native + JS fallback) plus the Reactivity-Lens sidecar, React→Pyreon migration, and project audits. Reverting `src/jsx.ts` (the JS path) is INVISIBLE to anything that goes through the native binary — the Rust path in `native/src/lib.rs` is a parallel implementation, kept byte-identical by the cross-backend equivalence tests. Edits to transform behavior must land in BOTH; the equivalence suite is the gate.
- [@pyreon/runtime-dom](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/runtime-dom): DOM renderer, mount, hydrateRoot, Transition, TransitionGroup, KeepAlive, SVG/MathML namespace, custom elements. SVG and MathML elements ALWAYS use `setAttribute()` for prop forwarding, never property assignment. Many SVG properties (`markerWidth`, `refX`, etc.) are read-only `SVGAnimatedLength` getters — `el[key] = value` crashes. Detected by `el.namespaceURI !== "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"`.
- [@pyreon/runtime-server](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/runtime-server): SSR/SSG VNode→HTML renderer — renderToString, renderToStream (out-of-order Suspense), per-request ALS context/store isolation. Signal accessors are called synchronously to snapshot their value — no effects are created. A `{count()}` expression renders the value at render time; it only becomes live after client hydration. SSR is one-shot.
- [@pyreon/router](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/router): hash+history+memory+SSR, context-based, prefetching, guards, loaders, useIsActive, View Transitions, middleware, typed search params. Off by default: a transition defers the DOM swap to the next frame and leaves the page un-hit-testable while it animates. Turn on with `createRouter({ viewTransition: true })` or per route with `meta.viewTransition: true` (`false` opts a route out). With it on, `await router.push()` resolves after `updateCallbackDone` (DOM commit), NOT after animation finishes. It does NOT wait for `.finished` (~200-300ms). `.ready` and `.finished` get empty `.catch()` handlers so `AbortError: Transition was skipped` rejections (from interrupted transitions) do not leak as unhandled promise rejections.
- [@pyreon/head](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/head): Reactive `<head>` tag management — useHead(), HeadProvider, renderWithHead() for SSR. Tags with the same key replace each other (innermost wins). Meta keys: `name` → `property` → index. Link keys: `href + rel` → `rel` → index. Script keys: `src` → index. Style and noscript are unkeyed and always accumulated.
- [@pyreon/schedule](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/schedule): Recurrence, business time and availability as plain data: RFC 5545 rules that stay on the wall clock across DST, working hours, free slots. A monthly rule on the 31st has no occurrence in April, June, September and November (RFC 5545 section 3.3.10). `add("2026-01-31", { months: 1 })` clamps to the 28th. They differ on purpose: a calendar rule says "the 31st", an add says "about a month later". For "the last day of every month" use `monthDays: [-1]`.
- [@pyreon/calendar](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/calendar): An event calendar and scheduler: event model, recurrence and time zones, month and time-grid layout. A one-day all-day event on the 18th ends on the 19th (`allDay("2026-11-18")` makes the pair). A timed event that ends exactly at midnight does not appear on the next day. An all-day event whose end equals its start is treated as one day; a timed one is a moment.
- [@pyreon/server](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/server): SSR + SSG + island architecture — createHandler(), prerender(), island(), serverIsland(), middleware chain. `mode: "stream"` uses `renderToStream` with shell + app + tail emission; Suspense boundaries resolve out-of-order. The `<head>` collected via `@pyreon/head` is flushed in the shell before any Suspense boundaries resolve, so async-loaded data does not contribute to it.
- [@pyreon/primitives](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/primitives): 22 canonical cross-platform UI primitives that compile to DOM + SwiftUI + Compose from one .tsx: Stack, Inline, Layer, Scroll, Spacer (layout); Text, Heading, Image, Audio, Video, Icon (content); Button, Press, Link, Gesture (interaction); Canvas + CanvasRect/CanvasCircle/CanvasLine/CanvasPath/CanvasText (drawing); Field, Toggle, Select, Modal (input); Tabs (+ Tab entries), Split (navigation). Plus <Transition>/<TransitionGroup> (animation), <WebView> (host a web-only component natively, bidirectional bridge) and <Web>/<NativeIOS>/<NativeAndroid> escape hatches.
- [@pyreon/sized-map](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/sized-map): Bounded Map<K, V> — evicts the oldest entry at a maxEntries cap; FIFO (default) or LRU-on-read mode. FIFO fits hot paths where a per-read recency bump (a `delete` + `set` pair) would dominate the real work (runtime-dom `_tplCache`, router loader/component caches). LRU-on-read fits caches where frequently-read entries must survive small caps (rocketstyle `_rsMemo`, `@pyreon/lint` AstCache, `@pyreon/zero` ISR `createMemoryStore`).

## UI system

- [@pyreon/ui-core](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/ui-core): Unified `PyreonUI` provider (theme + mode + config), `useMode()` hook, init() escape hatch. The legacy split (separate theme / mode / config providers) is removed. `PyreonUI` is the only correct mount; calling `init()` directly is the escape hatch for SSR or test environments where the provider tree is unavailable.
- [@pyreon/styler](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/styler): CSS-in-JS — styled() / css / keyframes / createGlobalStyle, reactive theming, FNV-1a-deduped StyleSheet (SSR-safe). The `css` tagged template yields a `CSSResult` (resolved on use, never injected by itself); `keyframes` stringifies to an animation NAME and injects its `@keyframes` rule at CALL time; `createGlobalStyle` returns a `ComponentFn` — a fully static template injects at call time, a dynamic one when the component mounts.
- [@pyreon/unistyle](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/unistyle): Responsive breakpoints, CSS property mappings, unit utilities, theme enrichment. Every visual package (`elements`, `rocketstyle`, `coolgrid`, `kinetic`) reads breakpoints / spacing / unit conventions from this package. Override defaults via `enrichTheme()` once at the app root rather than per-component.
- [@pyreon/elements](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/elements): Five foundational layout primitives — Element, Text, List, Overlay, Portal — plus the useOverlay positioning hook and the Iterator data helper. A one-off look is a named `.multiple()` modifier on the rocketstyle component (`Grid.multiple({ threeUp: { gridTemplateColumns: { md: "repeat(3, 1fr)" } } })` → `<Grid multiple="threeUp" />`), typed and resolved through the theme. `css` (Element `css` / `contentCss` / `beforeContentCss` / `afterContentCss`, Text `css`) is only for a selector or an at-rule: a `css` tagged-template result or a `(css) => css`…`` callback, per breakpoint or as an array; a raw string does not type-check (and renders with a one-time dev warning when a cast or `h()` lets one through). It renders into `@layer instance`, declared after `@layer elements` (base layout) and `@layer rocketstyle` (`.theme()`): `@layer elements, rocketstyle, instance;`, so it beats the component theme, pseudo-classes included; unlayered CSS beats every layer. Lint: `pyreon/prefer-style-modifier` (warn) flags `css` on a component, `pyreon/no-raw-css-string` (error) flags raw CSS text.
- [@pyreon/attrs](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/attrs): Chainable HOC factory — default props (.attrs), base swaps (.config), HOC composition (.compose), statics (.statics). 'priority' does NOT mean 'highest precedence' — priorityAttrs resolve FIRST (so later .attrs() callbacks can read them as input) but sit at the LOWEST precedence in the final merge: priorityAttrs < attrs < explicit props. @pyreon/rocketstyle uses the slot to seed structural base props the dimension layer can still override.
- [@pyreon/rocketstyle](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/rocketstyle): Multi-dimensional component styling — states, sizes, variants, custom dimensions, dark/light mode, all cached. useBooleans defaults to FALSE — dimension props take strings (state="primary"), not boolean shorthands. Historically the TYPE default said true while the runtime was false, so boolean props typechecked but were silently dropped; the runtime default (false) is now authoritative in both.
- [@pyreon/coolgrid](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/coolgrid): Context-cascading responsive grid — Container, Row, Col with custom columns and breakpoints. Every numeric grid prop (size/gap/gutter/padding/columns) is responsive — a single number, a mobile-first array ([12, 6, 4]), or a breakpoint-keyed object ({ xs: 12, md: 6 }); size 0 hides the column at that breakpoint.
- [@pyreon/kinetic](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/kinetic): CSS-transition animations — kinetic(tag) chainable factory, 4 modes (transition/collapse/stagger/group), SSR-safe (peer: @pyreon/core, @pyreon/reactivity, @pyreon/runtime-dom). A transition whose `show` is false at server render still emits its children with the hidden-state class/style inlined (`leaveTo` if defined, else `enterFrom`) — content is structural, animation is visual (Framer Motion / react-transition-group norm). Load-bearing for SSG scroll-reveal where IntersectionObserver can't fire server-side. Trade-off: an INITIALLY-HIDDEN transition with `unmount: true` stays in the DOM (leave-to class applied) after a later leave; initially-visible transitions keep the true-unmount semantic.
- [@pyreon/kinetic-presets](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/kinetic-presets): 122 animation presets + 5 configurable factories + 5 composition utilities for @pyreon/kinetic. Tree-shaking is first-class: an internal #__NO_SIDE_EFFECTS__ annotation on the preset factory plus sideEffects: false means importing one named preset ships ~300 bytes — importing the `presets` map pins all 122.
- [@pyreon/connector-document](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/connector-document): Bridge between ui-system JSX trees and @pyreon/document — extracts a DocNode tree for multi-format export. Extraction is a snapshot — reactive accessor children and function-valued `_documentProps` are resolved (called) at extraction time, not subscribed; re-run `extractDocumentTree` after a signal change to export the live state.
- [@pyreon/document-primitives](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/document-primitives): 18 rocketstyle document components — render in browser AND export to 20 formats via the same tree. `DocDocument` `title` / `author` / `subject` accept either strings or `() => string` accessors. Function values are stored in `_documentProps` and resolved by `extractDocumentTree` at extraction time, so each export click reads the LIVE value from any underlying signal — no `const initial = get()` workaround needed.

## Ecosystem packages

- [@pyreon/http](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/http): Transport layer under @pyreon/query — onion middleware, typed errors, optional schema validation (peer: @pyreon/validation). Deliberate. @pyreon/query already retries 3×, so a client-side default of 3 turns one logical query into NINE requests with nothing in devtools to explain it. Opt in with `use: [retry()]` and keep the total visible in one place.
- [@pyreon/hooks](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/hooks): 65 signal-based hooks: state (useToggle/useCounter/usePrevious/useLatest/useControllableState), DOM (useEventListener/useClickOutside/useFocus/useHover/useFocusTrap/useFocusReturn/useInertOthers/useElementSize/useWindowResize/useWindowScroll/useScrollLock/useIntersection/useInfiniteScroll), responsive (useBreakpoint/useMediaQuery/useColorScheme/useSizeClass/useReducedMotion), timing (useDebouncedValue/useDebouncedCallback/useThrottledCallback/useInterval/useTimeout/useTimeAgo), interaction (), data (useFetch/useAuth/useDatabase/useGeolocation/useMap/useWebSocket/useSecureStorage/usePush/usePayments), composition (useMergedRef/useUpdateEffect/useIsomorphicLayoutEffect). `useControllableState({ value, defaultValue, onChange })` is the canonical controlled/uncontrolled pattern. Every primitive in `@pyreon/ui-primitives` uses it. Reimplementing the `isControlled + signal + getter` shape by hand was the #1 anti-pattern across primitives before the helper landed. Pass `value` as a FUNCTION (`() => props.checked`) so the controlled prop read tracks reactively; `defaultValue` is a PLAIN value captured once as the uncontrolled initial.
- [@pyreon/store](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/store): Global state management — Pinia-inspired composition stores returning StoreApi<T>. Stores are singletons by ID — the setup function runs once. Calling the returned hook multiple times returns the same StoreApi instance. Use `resetStore(id)` or `resetAllStores()` to force re-creation.
- [@pyreon/money](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/money): Exact amounts of money as plain data: decimal-string amounts, bigint math, nine rounding modes, allocation that never loses a cent. A `number` is read by its shortest round-trip text, so `money(9.99, "EUR")` is exactly 9.99. A number (or string) with more decimals than the currency has throws unless `rounding` is given: `money(0.1 + 0.2, "EUR")` is `0.30000000000000004`, which is floating-point noise, not an amount. Trailing zeros that lose nothing (`"9.990"`) are accepted.
- [@pyreon/state-tree](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/state-tree): Structured reactive state tree — composable models with snapshots, patches, and middleware. State mutations must go through actions — direct `.set()` calls on state signals bypass middleware and patch recording. The model enforces this in dev mode.
- [@pyreon/form](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/form): Signal-based form management with fields, validation, arrays, and cross-field watchers. Fields validate on blur by default so users aren't scolded mid-keystroke. Use `validateOn: "change"` for instant feedback (often paired with `debounceMs: 300` to avoid thrashing async validators), or `validateOn: "submit"` for zero-feedback-until-submit forms. `showError` (from `useField`) gates on `touched`, so even with `validateOn: "change"` errors won't appear until the user has blurred at least once — this is intentional.
- [@pyreon/upload](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/upload): File selection, validation, preview and upload with progress as signals: a queue with retry, pause and concurrency, real XHR progress, drop and picker state. Size, type and sniffing checks make the interface friendly; they do not protect the server, because a client can send anything. The server must check type, size and content itself, and must never trust the file name or the declared type.
- [@pyreon/validation](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/validation): The library-agnostic validation gate — Standard Schema bridge + Zod / Valibot / ArkType adapters. Zero runtime dependencies — the one dependency is the types-only `@standard-schema/spec` (the Standard Schema contract's official type, erased at build), and there are no peer-dependency records: schema libraries are detected by duck-typing the `~standard` (Standard Schema) contract. Install only the one you use — the adapters are tree-shaken per import path (`@pyreon/validation/zod`, `@pyreon/validation/valibot`, `@pyreon/validation/arktype`).
- [@pyreon/validate](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/validate): Pyreon's own validation library — chainable + function-comp hybrid API, Standard Schema-native, with built-in field metadata, reactive parse, and i18n-aware error formatting. The protocol deliberately omits a metadata channel — that's the gap `withField` fills. The protocol also doesn't carry i18n keys — `formatErrors` adds that layer.
- [@pyreon/query](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/query): TanStack Query adapter with signal-driven results + WebSocket subscriptions + SSE (useSSE). `useQuery` / `useInfiniteQuery` / `useQueries` / `useSuspenseQuery` take options as a FUNCTION (not an object) so `queryKey` and other fields can read Pyreon signals. TanStack core uses an object; Pyreon wraps so changing a tracked signal re-runs the observer options and refetches automatically.
- [@pyreon/table](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/table): Pyreon adapter for TanStack Table — reactive options, signal-driven state, flexRender. Options must be a FUNCTION `() => TableOptions<T>`, not a plain object. Signal reads inside the function are tracked reactively — changing any tracked signal re-syncs the table automatically.
- [@pyreon/virtual](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/virtual): Pyreon adapter for TanStack Virtual — element-scoped and window-scoped virtualization. Both hooks return reactive signals (`virtualItems()`, `totalSize()`, `isScrolling()`). Always read them inside reactive scopes (JSX thunks, effect, computed) so they update on scroll.
- [@pyreon/i18n](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/i18n): Reactive i18n with Intl number/date/relative-time formatting, plurals, interpolation, async namespaces. `@pyreon/i18n` includes JSX components (Trans, I18nProvider, useI18n) and depends on `@pyreon/core`. `@pyreon/i18n/core` is framework-agnostic with only `@pyreon/reactivity` as a dependency — use it for backends and edge workers.
- [@pyreon/feature](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/feature): Schema-driven CRUD primitives — define once, get queries, forms, tables, and stores. defineFeature composes 5 packages internally (@pyreon/query, @pyreon/form, @pyreon/validation, @pyreon/store, @pyreon/table). All must be installed, and a QueryClient provider must be mounted in the component tree for the query hooks to work.
- [@pyreon/a11y](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/a11y): Accessibility primitives — announce() screen-reader live regions, <VisuallyHidden>, createA11yId, zero setup
- [@pyreon/ambient](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/ambient): The ambient values every formatted thing depends on: locale, time zone and a shared clock with self-updating tickers (peer: @pyreon/core, @pyreon/reactivity). On a server nothing ticks: `useNow()` returns the plain read, which is the `provideClock` instant when one is provided and `Date.now()` otherwise. Provide the render instant per request and emit it with `clockScript()` or `clockAttributes()`; otherwise a relative time such as "2 sec ago" can differ between the server HTML and the first client render. Capturing the instant automatically at the first read of a request needs a request-scoped store in `@pyreon/runtime-server`, which does not exist yet.
- [@pyreon/charts](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/charts): Pyreon's own charting engine: marks as JSX children, typed channels, canvas and SVG, the same chart on the web, iOS and Android. `@pyreon/charts` is the stable surface: `<Chart>`, its marks, the family components, formatters, theme and linking. `/svg` renders charts to SVG strings with no DOM. `/engine` exports every layout, hit test and draw-list builder for building on the engine, and is not covered by the stability promise.
- [@pyreon/charts-maps](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/charts-maps): Boundary data for @pyreon/charts maps — world countries and US states as TopoJSON, one lazy module per map. A `MapModule` carries `projection`, `nameProperty` and `idProperty`; `<MapChart map={module}>` uses them, and any value you pass in `options` overrides the matching default.
- [@pyreon/auth](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/auth): OIDC sign-in on web, iOS and Android, ID-token verification, sessions, TOTP and passkeys — secure by default
- [@pyreon/storage](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/storage): Reactive client-side storage — localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies, IndexedDB. Browser-backed hooks (`useStorage`, `useSessionStorage`, `useIndexedDB`) return the default value on the server. `useCookie` is SSR-readable via `setCookieSource()` which reads from the request headers. Under `@pyreon/runtime-server` the signal registry is isolated per request automatically, so concurrent renders never share a cached signal — pass an ACCESSOR cookie source bound to your request context to make use of it.
- [@pyreon/sync](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/sync): Local-first CRDT-backed sync for signals — a synced signal IS a signal, so a remote op drives ONE fine-grained DOM update, not a re-render. `@pyreon/sync` (core bridge — engine-free, universal), `@pyreon/sync/yjs` (real Yjs engine + transports + persistence + collaborative text/lists — pulls in `yjs`), `@pyreon/sync/server` (Node/Bun relay — pulls in `ws` + `node:http`, never import into client code).
- [@pyreon/hotkeys](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/hotkeys): Keyboard shortcut management — scope-aware, modifier keys, conflict detection. By default, shortcuts do NOT fire when focused on form elements (input, textarea, select, contenteditable). Pass `enableOnInputs: true` in options to override. Escape is a common candidate for this override.
- [@pyreon/command](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/command): A command palette for Pyreon: a fuzzy matcher, a registry of commands with shortcuts, recents and nested pages. The matcher finds subsequences. A letter that is missing is fine ("prjct" finds "Project"); a letter that is transposed or wrong is not corrected ("porject" does not).
- [@pyreon/permissions](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/permissions): Reactive permissions — RBAC, ABAC, feature flags, subscription tiers. `admin.*` matches exactly one segment (`admin.users`, not `admin.users.list`); use `admin.**` to match any depth below `admin`, and `*` for everything. Resolution is most-specific-first, so an exact or `**` deny overrides a broader subtree grant.
- [@pyreon/machine](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/machine): Reactive state machines — constrained signals with type-safe transitions. Unlike XState, Pyreon machines have no built-in context. Use regular signals alongside the machine for associated data — the machine handles the state transitions, signals handle the data.
- [@pyreon/flow](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/flow): Reactive flow diagrams — signal-native nodes, edges, pan/zoom, auto-layout with its own engine (no layout dependency) (peer: @pyreon/runtime-dom). LayoutOptions.direction / layerSpacing / edgeRouting apply to layered/tree only — force/stress/radial/box/rectpacking silently ignore them. nodeSpacing is the only field respected by every algorithm. Dev-mode console.warn fires when an option is set on an algorithm that ignores it.
- [@pyreon/format](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/format): Locale-aware formatting and parsing — numbers, currency, bytes, durations, lists, dates, relative time — as plain functions over Intl with bounded caches (peer: @pyreon/core, @pyreon/reactivity). This package is Experimental: the API may change in a minor release before it is promoted to Stable.
- [@pyreon/code](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/code): Reactive code editor — CodeMirror 6 with signals, minimap, diff editor, lazy-loaded languages (peer: @pyreon/runtime-dom). `@pyreon/runtime-dom` is required in consumer apps because `<CodeEditor>` JSX emits `_tpl()` / `_bind()` calls.
- [@pyreon/rich-text](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/rich-text): Reactive WYSIWYG editor — signal-backed layer over TipTap (ProseMirror), lazy-loaded, a11y-labeled (peer: @pyreon/runtime-dom). `@pyreon/runtime-dom` is required in consumer apps because `<RichText>` JSX emits `_tpl()` / `_bind()` calls.
- [@pyreon/document](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/document): Universal document rendering — 18 primitives, 20 output formats. Heavy format renderers are lazy-loaded: PDF (~3MB via pdfmake + bundled fonts), DOCX (~700KB via docx), XLSX (~1.1MB via exceljs), PPTX (~400KB via pptxgenjs). First render of each format triggers the dynamic import; subsequent renders are instant. The engines are optional peer dependencies, so an app installs only the ones for the formats it renders, and bundlers ship only the renderers it invokes.
- [@pyreon/rx](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/rx): Signal-aware reactive transforms — filter, map, flatMap, sortBy, groupBy, countBy, pipe, debounce, throttle, 42 functions. Detection is purely `typeof source === "function"` (see `isSignal` in `rx/src/types.ts`) — there is NO `.subscribe` / value inspection. Any function (the signal, an accessor wrapper `() => items()`, a bound method) is treated as reactive and called inside a computed. The actual mistake is the opposite of what you might expect: passing a RESOLVED value (`items()`, an already-read array) takes the static path and never updates. Pass the signal, not its resolved value.
- [@pyreon/time](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/time): Dates and times as plain strings and numbers: ISO values, DST-correct zone math, calendar grids, no classes (peer: @pyreon/core, @pyreon/reactivity). PlainDate `YYYY-MM-DD` (year 0001-9999, a real day); PlainYearMonth `YYYY-MM`; PlainTime `HH:MM`, `HH:MM:SS` or `HH:MM:SS.f` to `.fff` (hour 00-23, second 00-59, no `24:00`, no leap second); PlainDateTime a PlainDate, an upper-case `T`, a PlainTime. No offsets or zone names, no lower-case `t`, no space separator, no unpadded fields: `isPlainDate("2026-2-3")` is false. Temporal accepts more; this package is strict so a value is always canonical and `compare` can be a string comparison. `parseInstant` is the one parser for timestamps with an offset.
- [@pyreon/toast](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/toast): Toast notifications — toast(), toast.success/error/warning/info/loading, Toaster component, a11y (peer: @pyreon/runtime-dom). Unlike most Pyreon packages, toast uses a module-level signal store — `toast()` works from event handlers, effects, or any non-component code. The `<Toaster />` component reads from this shared store.
- [@pyreon/url-state](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/url-state): URL-synced state — useUrlState(key, default) or schema mode, auto type coercion, SSR-safe. Type coercion is based on the default value: `useUrlState("page", 1)` coerces `?page=2` to number `2`. `useUrlState("page", "1")` keeps it as string `"1"`. Always provide the right type as default.
- [@pyreon/dnd](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/dnd): Signal-driven drag and drop over @atlaskit/pragmatic-drag-and-drop — draggable, droppable, sortable, file drop, monitor. The element-bound hooks (`useDraggable` / `useDroppable` / `useFileDrop`) defer pdnd registration to the next microtask so `ref` callbacks are populated first — call the hook in the component body and let the ref land. `useDragMonitor` registers immediately (it has no element to wait for).

## Tools

- [@pyreon/storybook](https://pyreon.dev/docs/storybook): Storybook renderer for Pyreon components
- [@pyreon/mcp](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/mcp): Model Context Protocol server — discoverability map, live API lookup, validation, migration, anti-pattern catalog, changelog, test-environment audit. Each `createServer()` instance maintains its own cached context (routes, components, islands). The cache auto-resets when `process.cwd()` changes between tool invocations, so the same server can operate across multiple projects in one session.
- [@pyreon/lint](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/lint): Pyreon-specific linter — 144 rules across 26 categories, config files, watch mode, AST cache, CLI + LSP
- [@pyreon/atlas](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/atlas): AI-native component workbench — derives, verifies, and serves a machine-readable component catalog
- [@pyreon/loom](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/loom): Monorepo dependency observatory — workspace graph, version-sync drift, cycles, phantom deps, and blast radius, as data
- [@pyreon/lathe](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/lathe): OpenAPI in, typed Pyreon client out — schemas, endpoints, queries, mocks, faker factories, Markdown reference and Atlas scenarios, with a multiplatform mode that proves its own output lowers to Swift and Kotlin
- [@pyreon/config](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/config): One `pyreon.config.ts` for the whole ecosystem — a typed section per package
- [@pyreon/testing](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/testing): Testing-Library-compatible test kit for Pyreon — render/cleanup/renderHook + the full @testing-library/dom surface + reactive-graph matchers (peer: @pyreon/runtime-dom, @pyreon/reactivity). The main `@pyreon/testing` entry does NOT auto-register `afterEach(cleanup)`. Add `@pyreon/testing/vitest` to your vitest `setupFiles` to wire auto-cleanup AND extend `expect` with jest-dom matchers; otherwise call `cleanup()` manually in `afterEach`.

## Zero (full-stack framework)

- [@pyreon/zero](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/zero): Full-stack meta-framework: fs-routing, SSR/SSG/ISR/SPA, API routes, server actions, adapters, i18n. mode: 'ssg' returns Plugin[] (the SSG plugin auto-attaches a companion `ssgPlugin()`); Vite's plugins array flattens nested arrays so `plugins: [pyreon(), zero()]` works as-is.
- [@pyreon/zero-content](https://pyreon.dev/docs/reference/zero-content): Compile-time .md/.mdx → Pyreon JSX, typed content collections, convention-scanned MDX components
